title: Post mortem for Lantern Orbit (subscriber paywall)
text:

Blameless review of PRJ00001, delivered with the Scaled Agile Release Train workflow.

title: Post mortem for Tidal Tributary (laboratory data capture service)
text:
# Post Mortem: Tidal Tributary (laboratory data capture service)
Blameless review of PRJ00003, delivered with the Stage Gate Phased Delivery workflow.
Outcome score 0.75.
## What went well
The lifecycle suited the problem; ceremonies and gates felt proportionate rather than bureaucratic.
## What did not go well
A data protection impact assessment was completed retrospectively after the data protection officer intervened. Penetration testing found critical vulnerabilities two days before launch, forcing a delayed release. Disagreement with the vendor over defects consumed weeks of management time.
## Lessons and recommended workflow adjustments
Insert a privacy impact assessment gate wherever personal data processing changes. Add an independent security review state before release with a named security approver. Add a vendor acceptance checkpoint with contract conformance evidence.

title: Post mortem for Vantage Ledger (admissions decision workflow)
text:
# Post Mortem: Vantage Ledger (admissions decision workflow)
Blameless review of PRJ00004, delivered with the Scaled Agile Release Train workflow.
Outcome score 0.99.
## What went well
The chosen workflow matched the nature of the work and the team settled into a steady rhythm. Regular accessibility review kept the service compliant with WCAG 2.2 AA. A weekly dependency sync surfaced blockers before they affected the plan. The dedicated security review gate caught injection flaws before they reached production. Regular demonstrations kept the broad stakeholder group aligned.
## What did not go well
Retention rules were missed because privacy was not considered until the final week.
## Lessons and recommended workflow adjustments
Include assistive technology testing in the definition of done for public journeys. Schedule a weekly cross team dependency sync with automatic escalation of blocked items. Require a model card and validation report before promotion to production. Make the data protection officer an approver on transitions that change personal data handling. Add an independent security review state before release with a named security approver. Invite every business owner to a demo at least monthly.

title: Post mortem for Amber Signal (policy renewal engine)
text:
# Post Mortem: Amber Signal (policy renewal engine)
Blameless review of PRJ00917, delivered with the Agile Scrum Product Delivery workflow.
Outcome score 0.55.
## What went well
Two full dress rehearsals made the live cutover uneventful. Automatic escalation of blocked dependencies kept work moving across teams. Soak testing at twice the forecast peak gave the team confidence for launch. The privacy impact assessment state ensured lawful basis and retention were settled before build.
## What did not go well
The workflow was a poor fit and the team spent considerable effort working around it. There was no tested rollback path when the deployment went wrong. Security findings surfaced late because no explicit security review state existed in the workflow.
## Lessons and recommended workflow adjustments
Rehearse the full migration at production volumes at least twice. Schedule a weekly cross team dependency sync with automatic escalation of blocked items. Make load test results a required artifact on the release transition. Insert a privacy impact assessment gate wherever personal data processing changes. Make the rollback plan a mandatory field on the release transition. Add an independent security review state before release with a named security approver.

# Post Mortem: Harbour Harvest 900 (outage management system)
Blameless review of PRJ01090, delivered with the Change Controlled Operations workflow.
Outcome score 0.91.
## What went well
The lifecycle suited the problem; ceremonies and gates felt proportionate rather than bureaucratic. Two full dress rehearsals made the live cutover uneventful. Soak testing at twice the forecast peak gave the team confidence for launch. Requiring a rollback plan improved release quality overall. Security engineers reviewing each release kept findings small and cheap to fix. Formal vendor acceptance checkpoints kept the supplier accountable.
## What did not go well
No significant delivery problems were recorded.
## Lessons and recommended workflow adjustments
Rehearse the full migration at production volumes at least twice. Add a performance testing stage against forecast peak demand before release. Require a tested rollback plan before any production release. Add an independent security review state before release with a named security approver. Track vendor milestones as states rather than in a separate spreadsheet.

title: Post mortem for Beacon Orbit 900 (number porting service)
text:
# Post Mortem: Beacon Orbit 900 (number porting service)
Blameless review of PRJ02207, delivered with the Kanban Continuous Flow workflow.
Outcome score 0.27.
## What went well
Requiring acceptance criteria before work began improved predictability. The privacy impact assessment state ensured lawful basis and retention were settled before build.
## What did not go well
Process friction was the most common theme in retrospectives. Model performance in production fell well below the offline estimate. Security findings surfaced late because no explicit security review state existed in the workflow. Open ended exploration consumed the budget before any result was usable.
## Lessons and recommended workflow adjustments
Introduce a definition of ready guard before work enters delivery. Add an independent model validation gate covering bias, drift and performance. Make the data protection officer an approver on transitions that change personal data handling. Treat security review as a workflow gate rather than an optional checklist item. Define kill criteria before starting an experiment.
